decisions.after: The officials said: "A name is tabooed at death, a feeling all share; hearing the name startles the heart, as earlier precepts also make clear.
decisions.reason: Retranslation is correct (Zuozhuan 名終將諱之; Liji 聞名心瞿) but 前誥 here refers to earlier canonical teachings being cited, not specifically imperial edicts; 'edicts' overclaims. 亦 restored as 'also'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 有司議云：「名終諱之，有心所同，聞名心瞿，亦明前誥。

decisions.after: Yet the Rites also say, 'In the ruler's presence there are no private taboos; in a grandee's presence there are public taboos'—that is, no private taboos.
decisions.reason: Liji quotation correctly rendered, but the trailing 無私諱 simply restates 'no private taboos'; 'private taboos yield' adds interpretation not in the text.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 而《禮》復云『君所無私諱，大夫之所有公諱』，無私諱。

decisions.after: It also says, 'There is no taboo in the Odes and the Documents, nor when handling written texts.'
decisions.reason: 詩書 in this Liji (Quli) quotation are the Odes and the Documents, not generic 'poems and documents'; 臨文 means when reading/writing texts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又云『詩書不諱，臨文不諱』。

decisions.reason: 公義奪私情，王制屈家禮 correctly rendered as a rhetorical exclamation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 豈非公義奪私情，王制屈家禮哉！

decisions.after: Your servant, Minister and Baron of Anzhong, earlier memorialized that the name of Wang You, Gentleman of the Central Troops Section, violated his father's taboo and that he asked to be relieved of office; a clear edict was issued permitting a change of section—an act of grace beyond the rules.
decisions.reason: Retranslation is basically right (王祐 Wang You; 中兵曹郎; 聽許換曹; 恩出制外), but it drops 臣, which marks the Minister as the memorialist speaking in his own voice, and its 'and asked to resign' leaves unclear who resigned (Wang You). Reading 先 as 'earlier' is kept, but 臣先 could also be title + 臣 + a personal name (Xian), so no personal name is supplied.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書安眾男臣先表中兵曹郎王祐名犯父諱，求解職，明詔爰發，聽許換曹，蓋是恩出制外耳。

decisions.reason: 頃者互相瞻式，源流既啟，莫知其極 correctly rendered.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 而頃者互相瞻式，源流既啟，莫知其極。

decisions.after: The imperial court's rites are great: the hundred officials fill their posts, offices are ranged in bureaus, and their business constantly crosses one another's.
decisions.reason: Proposed text omits 編官列署 (offices arrayed in bureaus); restored for completeness.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 夫皇朝禮大，百僚備職，編官列署，動相經涉。

decisions.reason: 移官易職，遷流莫已，既違典法，有虧政體 rendered accurately and concisely.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若以私諱，人遂其心，則移官易職，遷流莫已，既違典法，有虧政體。
